payload.feature:
LANDING PR for story #403, seventh landing (a timed-out attempt ends its whole process tree, and Claude descendants no longer keep working after a failure and retry).

The branch story-403-process-tree is on main 78938e53 and ends at 87b518bb. The sixth landing (landing-pr-for-story-403-sixth-l-809dd445) vouched for 4e5853a6 clean. PR #483's macOS CI on 4e5853a6 then passed 487 brokkr-protocol tests and failed one: a_recorded_descendant_whose_row_loses_its_stamp_parks_the_attempt read Table { "the ps row \"2216 1 2216 S\" could not be read" } where Signal { pid: 2216, ... } was expected.

The test plays macOS's ps on Linux through as_ps. Its grandchild is a job whose shell exits at once, and it is recorded only because the driver adopts it as subreaper. On real macOS the grandchild goes to launchd unrecorded (the row reads ppid 1). That is the residual the operator's ruling of 2026-09-28 accepted, so there is no identity kill to refuse, and the EPERM group's unreadable read is reported, as the sixth landing confirmed it should be. The controller's commit 87b518bb gates the test to Linux with that reason in its doc comment, beside a_job_orphaned_before_the_tracker_saw_it_is_ended_before_the_report. It changes no production code.

OPERATOR RULINGS (2026-09-28), binding: Linux is closed, apart from two accepted Linux residuals (the table-read race in all its orderings, and the read-to-fork instant) and the accepted macOS escape between two reads. Per-attempt cgroups (#472) close the Linux ones. The lows are in #470. None of these are findings.

Judge:
1. That 87b518bb is test-only, and that the gate is exactly the ruled macOS residual: the test's grandchild is recorded only through the Linux subreaper.
2. That the three tests now gated to Linux are the only ones whose behaviour is Linux-only by design or by ruling, and that the macOS table path (as_ps, kill_listed, the EPERM read) keeps a test that runs on macOS. Name it.
3. That every earlier landing's confirmation stands at this head.

This run lands one pull request under decision 0051 so the contribution gate can vouch for it. If a finding returns the branch, fix exactly that finding and prove it with a test bound by a compiling mutation. Then run cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy on the crates you touched with -D warnings, typos --hidden, and quality/ratchet.sh files and clones (all clean). Commit one signed-off commit ending "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", and never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read.

folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including both supported operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],
  "organization_profiles": [
    {"repository": "feedback-loop-ai/.github", "path": "profile/README.md", "project_url": "https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr", "apply": "after verified publication"}
  ],
  "channels": [
    {"name": "GitHub release", "evidence": "Four platform archives, Linux deb/rpm packages, SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance."},
    {"name": "crates.io", "evidence": "All seven workspace crates serve the new version."},
    {"name": "apt and rpm", "evidence": "The signed Pages repositories index the new packages."},
    {"name": "Homebrew and Nix", "evidence": "The generated channel PRs are merged and their versions and digests match the release manifest."}
  ],
  "extensions": [
    {"name": "workflow toolchain agreement", "instructions": "Check that CI, release admission and local coverage select the same pinned compiler.", "evidence": "Both workflows and coverage-exact.sh consume rust-nightly-version.txt."},
    {"name": "frozen contracts", "instructions": "Compare contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json and reference against the previous release; explain additive versions and flag modifications to frozen bytes.", "evidence": "A reviewed diff with migration notes for any new contract versions."}
```

members.adversarial: Adversarial, read-only review of the seventh landing of #403. Scope: the sole new commit 87b518bb over the sixth landing's vouched head 4e5853a6 (git rev-list --count 4e5853a6..HEAD = 1; git status --porcelain empty; nothing changed or committed by this seat). No production code changes. The gate is on the right test: its grandchild is a job (own_group) whose shell exits at once, and attempts.rs Live::record roots descendants only at the leader/recorded ppids and the attempt group; the job leaves the group and is reparented to its driver only on Linux, where attempts::detach calls subreaper() under cfg(target_os = "linux") (set_child_subreaper). On macOS there is no subreaper, so it reparents to launchd (ppid 1) and is never recorded; there is no recorded identity to signal, and the macOS CI failure (Unsettled::Table where Unsettled::Signal was expected) is exactly that path, not a fail-open. This matches tree.rs's header and the still-PROPOSED 0006 addendum's macOS residual text (a descendant that leaves the group and whose parent exits between two reads is reparented to launchd unseen). (2) Exactly three cfg(target_os = "linux") lines exist in process/tests.rs, on a_running_driver_adopts_its_trees_orphans (subreaper by design), a_job_orphaned_before_the_tracker_saw_it_is_ended_before_the_report (the ruled macOS residual) and a_recorded_descendant_whose_row_loses_its_stamp_parks_the_attempt (this commit); 87b518bb adds/removes no other cfg. The other Linux gates the story added are genuinely Linux-only helpers/tests (attempts/tests.rs:348 subreaper-zombie reap; table/tests.rs /proc parsing) and production cfg in table.rs/attempts.rs. The macOS table path keeps tests that run on macOS: a_group_refused_with_eperm_is_gone_only_when_the_table_shows_it_gone (attempts/tests.rs:480; the EPERM read, pinning Unread -> Unsettled::Table and identity-first Signal) and a_kill_by_listing_needs_the_row_whole (table/tests.rs:242; kill_listed refuses a stampless row), with the ps-parsing tests a_ps_row_keeps_its_start_time_whole / a_ps_row_flagged_e_reads_as_exiting / a_ps_row_without_its_start_time_is_not_read / a_failed_or_unparsed_ps_is_no_table. Observation, not a finding: as_ps is a Linux-side test double (it plays macOS ps over table::snapshot) and never executed on macOS, so gating its only caller loses no real-macOS coverage and removes no production assertion. a_grandchild_cannot_join_the_engines_group_to_outlive_the_report stays ungated and host-independent. (3) Earlier confirmations stand at this head: HEAD 87b518bb's parent is 4e5853a6 (sixth landing, clean) and 72c7937d (fifth landing) is an ancestor; every pre-rebase ledger head (second 391d4dbd, third/finish-story 0c9df16f, fourth a23f8dd3, rebase-and-finish edf539c7, fix-403-on-macos 3336859c, remediate fourth round fdd11101) is content-identical in added/removed lines to a commit in the current ancestry, and the fifth/sixth landings re-verified the rebased chain. Ran on this Linux host: cargo fmt --all -- --check exit 0; cargo clippy -p brokkr-protocol --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings exit 0; cargo test -p brokkr-protocol --lib --locked 502 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored (an initial run showed 15 failures solely because the harness exports a malformed GIT_CONFIG_COUNT with no GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0, breaking child git init; with that env cleared all pass); the six named tests each pass; typos --hidden exit 0; quality/ratchet.sh files 'file size holds' and clones 'duplication holds'. No concrete input -> wrong output found; the four ruled #403 residuals (Linux table-read race in all orderings, read-to-fork instant, accepted macOS escape) and the #470 lows are excluded by the operator's 2026-09-28 ruling and are not findings. macOS CI and the controller's exact-coverage gate are external to this seat. result.notes: Review chief for the seventh landing of #403 (run landing-pr-for-story-403-seventh-36e879ae). FLOOR: the panel reported residual at medium (correctness: residual, medium; adversarial: clean), so this seat rules residual with max_residual_severity medium and cannot rule clean. Nothing under notes addressed the gate, restated its instructions or argued for a result; both positions returned usable results. MY READ OF THE DIFF: the sole new commit 87b518bb over the sixth landing's vouched head 4e5853a6 (rev-list count 1; HEAD~1 is 4e5853a6; worktree clean before and after; 78938e53 is an ancestor) adds five lines to crates/brokkr-protocol/src/process/tests.rs: a Linux-only note in the doc comment and cfg(target_os = linux) on a_recorded_descendant_whose_row_loses_its_stamp_parks_the_attempt. No production code changes. (1) CONFIRMED: test-only, and the gate is exactly the ruled macOS residual. The test's grandchild plays the job role: role_driver's shell exits at once by design, and own_group moves the grandchild out of the attempt's group with setpgid. Live::record roots descendants only at recorded pids and the open attempt's group, so an out-of-group orphan is recorded only if its new parent is recorded. On Linux attempts::detach calls subreaper (set_child_subreaper, cfg linux), so the driver adopts the orphan and the tracker records it; on macOS there is no subreaper, the orphan goes to launchd (ppid 1) and is never recorded, so there is no recorded identity to refuse and the identity-first Signal cannot arise. The macOS CI reading of Unsettled::Table (the full-table read failed on the stripped row) is the fail-closed park of a table that cannot be read, not a fail-open; the escape it stands beside is the accepted 2026-09-28 macOS residual, stated at tree.rs:99-105 and in the still-PROPOSED 0006 addendum (line 195). The doc comment states that reason. (2) CONFIRMED: process/tests.rs carries exactly three Linux gates, a_running_driver_adopts_its_trees_orphans (subreaper, absent on macOS by design), a_job_orphaned_before_the_tracker_saw_it_is_ended_before_the_report (the ruled macOS residual) and this commit's test (the same residual); 87b518bb adds or removes no other cfg. The crate's other Linux gates are /proc parsing and subreaper reaping, Linux-only by design: an_orphan_that_exited_before_its_first_read_is_reaped (attempts/tests.rs:348), a_stat_line_is_read_from_its_last_parenthesis and a_row_that_cannot_be_read_fails_the_snapshot (table/tests.rs:92, :132). The macOS CI on 4e5853a6 passing every other brokkr-protocol test is the evidence that no further ungated test is Linux-only. a_grandchild_cannot_join_the_engines_group_to_outlive_the_report stays ungated. The macOS table path keeps tests that run on macOS, named: the EPERM group read is a_group_refused_with_eperm_is_gone_only_when_the_table_shows_it_gone (attempts/tests.rs:480), pinning gone-only-on-a-whole-read, Unread yielding to a recorded identity's refusal first (Signal) and otherwise the read's own failure (Table); kill_listed is a_kill_by_listing_needs_the_row_whole (table/tests.rs:242, a stampless row is returned unread and not signalled, a listed identity is killed) and a_kill_by_listing_spares_a_reused_pid (:273); ps parsing is a_ps_row_keeps_its_start_time_whole, a_ps_row_flagged_e_reads_as_exiting, a_ps_row_without_its_start_time_is_not_read and a_failed_or_unparsed_ps_is_no_table; the real macOS snapshot and kill through ps run in every ungated Host::REAL test. as_ps is a test double that plays macOS's ps on Linux over table::snapshot; it is not production code, and on macOS it would only re-parse the real ps. (3) CONFIRMED: every earlier landing's confirmation stands at this head, because the head differs from 4e5853a6 by test lines only; the sixth landing's ledger vouched 4e5853a6 clean with its exact-coverage gate green, and the fifth (72c7937d) is an ancestor. SURVIVING FINDINGS (one list for the implementer): [1] medium, author correctness (decision 0071 ruling 9): gating the test removes the only macOS caller of stampless_engine and as_ps, so no macOS-running test exercises as_ps through attempt cleanup, and criterion 2 is read as unmet. Carried at medium by the floor. On my read this finding does not identify a defect in the change: as_ps is a Linux-side double of macOS's ps, not a production path; the test was introduced in 5292a95c on this branch and has never passed on macOS, so no green macOS coverage is lost; the production macOS path keeps the macOS-running tests named above; and the end-to-end composition (recorded descendant, stampless row, identity kill carried, attempt parks) is exercised on Linux, where the exact-coverage gate runs.
